summary_for_children: Al-Insan means Man. It praises people who feed the needy, orphans and captives only for Allah, wanting no thanks.
environment_concept: An open doorway where food is shared (76:8).
architecture_and_scenery: A kitchen and doorway, baskets of food.

areas.name: The Doorway
areas.description: A doorway where food is shared.

activities.name: Share the meal
activities.description: Carry three loaves to the open door to share.

story_library.source: Owner's 'Quran Adventure — Children's Story Library' (2026-11-04), first-draft narration for ages about 7-12
story_library.title: The Gift of Kindness
story_library.children_narration: Surah Al-Insan reminds us that human beings are tested through choices. It praises people who give food to those in need, including the poor, orphans, and captives, without expecting a reward from them. True generosity can come from sincere care.

world_idea.title: The House of Giving
world_idea.description: Prepare food parcels, identify community needs, and learn why kindness matters even when no one is watching. Quranic descriptions of Paradise are studied respectfully, not reconstructed as fact.

story_library.checks: Every reference exists in the verified text (checked 2026-11-04). Narration is draft, written by the owner, not reviewed by a scholar.
story_library.rule_conflicts_resolved: Paradise passages (76:12-22) are readings only, not built.
